CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath that occurs with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up the driveway. Patient reports associated palpitations. Symptoms have been occurring more frequently lately. Patient is uncertain if symptoms are related to chronic back pain. Recently increased exercise activity to address weight gain. Smoking has decreased from two packs per day to approximately once per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other issues bothering her at this time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Smoking history

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression
Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: Currently smoking approximately once per day, down from two packs per day previously. Recently increased exercise activity. Has discussed doing yoga but has not made it a habit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Vital signs not mentioned. Lungs: Mild wheezes in all lung fields. Otherwise unremarkable.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests: Show possible asthma or COPD. Chest X-ray: Flattened diaphragm noted, consistent with COPD seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease): Patient diagnosed with COPD based on pulmonary function tests, chest X-ray findings, and physical examination. Start Combivent inhaler, two puffs twice daily. Prescribe albuterol inhaler, two puffs as needed for acute shortness of breath. Prescribe prednisone taper pack.
Depression: Stable. Continue Effexor. Encouraged to do yoga.
Chronic back pain: Continue Gabapentin (Neurontin). No changes to current management.
